thought: The 7th Company Commander is characterized as someone who studies orders under dim oil lamps with serious expression and firm gaze - suggesting a meticulous, studious, and intellectually rigorous approach to command. Among the existing characters, none wear glasses. Round wire-rimmed reading glasses would be highly distinctive, period-appropriate for 1941, and perfectly reinforce his character as a commander who carefully studies military orders and documents. This visual element immediately distinguishes him from the more physically-defined soldiers while suggesting his methodical, detail-oriented command style. As a company commander (连长), his rank falls between squad leaders and regiment commander, so he should have officer insignia but appear more field-weathered than the regiment commander.
distinctive_features: Round wire-rimmed reading glasses perched on his nose - unique among all characters and reflecting his studious, meticulous nature as someone who carefully studies military orders
